focus.headline: 📞 Marcos Oliveira / Indigo Road — 3:00pm CT. This is the highest-leverage call you've had. One yes = years of recurring work.
focus.ctx: Indigo Road is a brand-driven hospitality group with budget line items. Marcos is not a local owner deciding over lunch — he's a Senior Director with procurement authority. Your unfair advantage: your photo is still on the Horseshoe Canyon Ranch website from a prior shoot. That's not a coincidence, that's a talking point. Goal of this call: scope, fit, and lock a follow-up in-person walk-through date. Don't quote price unless he asks directly. Do not pitch the Entry Package. Anchor is $1,500–$2,000 destination brand video or $1,000–$1,500/mo retainer. Pick up at 2:58pm CT. Don't be late on a call with a corporate buyer.

checklist.text: Screenshot Matt Bell's endorsement comment + repost
checklist.sub: Do this BEFORE leaving · testimonial gold
checklist.ctx: Save the receipts before something happens to them. Open the FB post, screenshot Matt's full comment with his name and 'Director, Explore Harrison' visible. Save to camera roll AND to a folder called 'testimonials' on your computer. This quote becomes social proof for the next 12 months: lead deck slide, BVC landing page testimonial, pitch email signature line, IG bio rotation.

checklist.text: Final gear check · bag at the door by 11:30

checklist.ctx: Run the gear checklist one more time. Cards formatted in-camera, batteries charged (camera + spares + gimbal + lav), lens cloth, ND filters, talent release for Josh, shot list printed. Leave by 11:30 to be at Matt's by 12:00. Late = wrong tone for the day.

checklist.sub: Confirm shoot plan + EH posting permissions
checklist.ctx: Lock these with Matt before heading out: 1) Permission to cross-share live Stories to Explore Harrison feed during the shoot. 2) Which businesses beyond Neighbor's Mill he wants featured (food, retail, scenery). 3) Whether he wants to be in any frames. 4) EH posting timing for the polished cut Saturday. Use the chair time to show him the BTS plan and confirm he's good with it.

checklist.sub: @Bray.Films IG · downtown setup vibe · no Josh yet
checklist.ctx: First Story of the day. Setup energy. Coffee, gear in hand, Harrison sign or downtown frame. No Josh. Sets the day's frame for everyone watching. Cross-share to EH Story if Matt approved. Tag @exploreharrison.

checklist.sub: Tag @joshpray + @neighborsmill · this is when his audience finds out
checklist.ctx: The visibility unlock. Over-the-shoulder of you filming Josh's reaction or the food. Tag @joshpray, @neighborsmill, @exploreharrison. This Story is the moment Josh's audience can re-share to their followers. Make it watchable, not just a slate.

checklist.text: Get BTS phone footage of you working the gimbal
checklist.sub: 30 sec total · have Cary, Matt, or staff grab it
checklist.ctx: This is Friday's @Bray.Films comeback Reel. Don't film yourself, hand someone a phone. Cary, Matt, or staff. They get 5-10 second clips of you on the gimbal, framing a shot, working with Josh. Quantity over polish, you'll cut to 30 seconds. Without this footage, Friday's restart Reel doesn't exist.

checklist.sub: Tripod-locked · 50mm · Josh to camera · Matt's money clip
checklist.ctx: Single most important shot of the day. Don't move on after one good take. Get three. Different deliveries. Prompt Josh: 'In one line, why should someone come to Harrison?' Let him riff. This is what closes the EH polished cut Saturday and what gets used in every future Bray Films pitch about working with creators.
Closes the day's narrative on Stories. Builds anticipation for Friday's drop. Don't reveal the closing line. Just signal that something is coming. Tag @joshpray and @exploreharrison.

checklist.text: Send Josh raw clips after wrap
checklist.sub: WeTransfer or AirDrop · let him post first
checklist.ctx: Note to Josh: 'Sending you the raw clips from today in case you want to use anything on your feed. We're posting our cut Saturday. Tag us if you do anything with it!' Don't ask for a re-share. Give and tag. If he posts, his audience floods you. If he doesn't, you still have the content.

checklist.text: Confirm with Brett: BBQ photos EOD today or Friday
checklist.sub: Quick text · he already knows · just lock the timing
checklist.ctx: Brett knows the timing already. One-line confirmation: 'Hey Brett, photos are coming end of day or first thing tomorrow. Will text when they're up.' Holds the relationship without overpromising. Edit happens between shoot and bed if energy holds, otherwise Friday morning.

checklist.sub: Call tomorrow 4pm EST · don't decide morning-of
checklist.ctx: Decide tonight before sleep. Default ladder: single destination brand video ($1,500–$2,000) entry → if he wants ongoing content, civic retainer ($1,000–$1,500/mo). Anchor in EH + Toinette + Matt's fresh public endorsement. NEW LEVERAGE: Matt Bell publicly recommended Bray Films this week. Drop that on the call once. Don't pre-quote in writing.

intro.title: Stakes · Major AR creator · millions of followers
intro.body: Day-with-Josh content for Explore Harrison + @Bray.Films. Tied to Matt Bell. Biggest portfolio asset of the quarter.
intro.ctx: Three wins to walk away with: 1) a polished day-in-the-life cut for Explore Harrison, 2) a BTS reel for @Bray.Films that positions you as 'the guy major creators work with,' 3) a screenshot of engagement at 24/48/72 hours to paste into pitch decks for the next 90 days. If you only nail one shot: the closing line, Josh to camera, single take, single line about Harrison. That's Matt's money clip.

gear.text: Prime lens for talking head (35 or 50mm)
Gimbal charged + balanced w/ mounted plate
Wireless lav for Josh + receiver charged
Phone running voice memos as audio backup
Notebook w/ shot list + questions printed
Cash/card for coffee + Josh's tab if it comes up

shots.body: Wide downtown waking up. Welcome-to-Harrison sign. Josh walking into frame from his car. Hands shot, keys, coffee, getting set up.
shots.ctx: Why these: Sets the 'outsider arrives' arc. Establishes time and place fast. The walking-in shot is your edit's opening frame, treat it like a movie cold open. Golden hour if Josh is up early, otherwise mid-morning is fine, you can grade it warm in post.

shots.body: Wide exterior with Josh entering. Mid shot ordering, talking with Cary. Detail shots: hands plating, food close-ups, steam, bread coming out. OTS first-bite reaction (the money clip). Cary cameo if available.
shots.ctx: This is the spine of the piece. Food + reaction + the local story (remodel, family business). Get three takes of the first bite from different angles, you'll thank yourself in the edit. Cary cameo: if he's around, frame him as 'the guy who built this,' Josh meets local. Don't over-direct, authentic reactions are the content.

shots.scene: 🌲 Outdoor / Nature (if Josh is up for it)
shots.body: Overlook wide if accessible. Josh silhouette against the landscape. Walking-into-frame establishing. Trail movement gimbal shot.
shots.ctx: Read his energy. If he's tired or not into it, skip, don't force outdoor content for Explore Harrison's tourism angle if it comes off forced. Best fallback: Scenic 7 overlook 10 min from town, drive-up shot, no hike required. One hero frame is all you need, not a whole nature segment.

shots.body: 50mm prime, clean backdrop, shallow depth of field. Josh mid-frame, slight off-center. Eye-line just off-camera. Lav + on-camera shotgun both rolling.
shots.ctx: Pick a spot with character but not noise. Quiet corner of the Mill works (post-rush), or outside in shade if wind is low. Backdrop matters more than location, brick wall, exposed wood, blurred greenery. Frame him as authority, eye-line up, not down at.

shots.body: Between takes: Josh laughing, looking around. You working the gimbal (third-person, phone). Cary or staff watching the shoot. 5-10 sec clips, get a lot of them.
shots.ctx: BTS is your @Bray.Films portfolio piece, not Explore Harrison's. Get a friend or Cary to grab phone footage of you working. This is what positions you as the guy major creators come to. Quantity over polish, these post fast, no edit needed.

shots.body: Josh to camera, single take, single line. Tripod-locked, 50mm, eye-line dead-center. This is Matt's money clip and Explore Harrison's hero frame.
shots.ctx: This is the ONE shot you can't miss. Get it three times minimum, even if Josh nails the first take. Different deliveries, slight variations. No cuts in the final use, single-take builds trust with the viewer. Prompt: 'In one line, why should someone come to Harrison?' Let him riff.

questions: What would you tell someone who's never been here?
What are you coming back for?
If you had a free Saturday in Harrison, where would you spend it?
What's the one place everyone watching should put on their list?
joshPrep.questionsCtx: Rules: Ask one question, then shut up. Let silence do the work. Josh is a creator, he'll fill it with gold if you don't talk over him. Don't read questions off paper, make it conversational. Pick 3-4, not all 5. Save the others as backup if a topic doesn't land. Total interview under 10 minutes, the closing line takes more attention than 10 long answers.

angles.title: Camera angles + storytelling angles
angles.body: Both matter. Camera shapes how he feels on screen. Story shapes why people watch.
angles.ctx:
Camera: Wide → medium → close progression on every scene. Eye-line up to Josh, not down at, frame him as authority not subject. OTS for reactions (puts viewer in the moment). Low angle for hero/landscape (makes him bigger than the scene). Lock-offs for talking head, no zooms or pans during answers. Handheld for BTS, intentional rawness. Single-take, no cuts on the closing line, that's a trust signal.

Story: The arc is 'outsider falls for Harrison.' First impressions → discoveries → recommendation. Neighbor's Mill is the spine. The food angle carries the middle. The 'real local, not a tourist trap' framing is your differentiator from generic travel content. Sequel hook for the second post: 'next time he's coming back for ___.'

social.title: Three feeds, three angles, every business tagged
social.body: Don't let this just be an Explore Harrison post. Tag every business. Coordinate with Josh on timing.
social.ctx:
Pre-shoot (today, Wed): Tease on @Bray.Films Story, 'big shoot tomorrow, don't sleep on Harrison.' Soft flag on Explore Harrison Story with Matt's permission.

Day of (Thu): Live Stories from set on @Bray.Films AND Explore Harrison. Tag Josh in every Story so he can re-share to his audience for free. 5-10 sec BTS clips throughout, post fast, no edit needed. One mid-day 'this is happening' post.

Post-shoot (Thu PM / Fri): Send Josh raw clips first, let him post first, you build off his momentum. Friday: @Bray.Films posts the BTS reel (Bentley working, gimbal in hand), this is YOUR portfolio piece. Saturday: Explore Harrison's polished cut goes live. Tag Josh + every business featured (Neighbor's Mill, Cary, etc.) in every post.

Strategic plays: Use Josh content as social proof in the Marcos call Friday afternoon. Screenshot engagement at 24, 48, 72 hours for future pitch decks. Add to lead-deck materials: 'Worked with Josh Pray on Explore Harrison content.' Repurpose 1-2 standout moments to personal feed (POV, hands working the gimbal, fits no-face floor). New BVC opener line: 'If Explore Harrison can land Josh Pray, your business can show up on this level too.'

philosophy.title: Posting Philosophy — IN PROGRESS
philosophy.sub: Cadence locked · paused at non-negotiables question
philosophy.body: Locked: 3 feeds, no on-camera Bentley until traction, no rebrand. Cadence: 2 Reels/wk → 3 once warmed. Personal IG/FB genuinely different (will converge later). Mainly new content, occasional rodeo throwback.
philosophy.ctx: Locked-in decisions: Three feeds (Bray.Films, Personal, Explore Harrison). No fourth thought-leader feed. No on-camera Bentley until serious traction. No rebrand. Floor without face: hands, gear, POV, scenery, food, places, family, voice-over over b-roll. Cadence (LOCKED May 5): @Bray.Films IG 2/wk → ramp to 3, plus Trial Reels for testing new styles. @Bray.Films FB: 1 long-form/wk + cross-post Reels. Personal IG: 1/wk curated. Personal FB: 1/wk personal-brand. NEXT: non-negotiables question waiting in chat.

floor.ctx: Why it matters: 'Just start posting on personal' feels weird because there's no rule for what counts. The floor IS the rule. If a post has hands, gear, POV, scenery, food, a place, family, or voice-over on b-roll, it's eligible. If not, skip it. Removes the daily decision tax.

decisions.title: Marcos Pricing Framing — decide TODAY for Friday call

decisions.body: What MUST hit each feed every week, no exceptions, even on a bad week? Three sub-questions waiting in chat.
decisions.ctx: My recommended floors: @Bray.Films IG = 1 Reel + 3 Stories. @Bray.Films FB = 1 cross-post. Personal IG = 1 post OR 3 Stories. Personal FB = 1 post (can be a phone photo with a real caption). Three sub-questions: 1) Are these floors too high or too low? 2) What's the ONE piece of content that, if missed, makes the week a failure? 3) Story posting on @Bray.Films, willing to commit to raw phone Stories, or off-brand?

northStar.title: North Star
northStar.body: Bray Films replaces ImpacTees as primary income. Solo video studio, owned brand, recurring revenue, freedom over schedule.
northStar.ctx: The replacement test: when Bray Films monthly recurring exceeds your ImpacTees paycheck consistently for 3 months, you have the leverage to reduce ImpacTees hours or fully exit. The math: ~5 retainers averaging $800/mo = $4,000/mo. Achievable in 12 months at current trajectory.

groups.name: 🌱 Inbound Watch · DO NOT OUTREACH YET
groups.ctx: Followed @bray.films FB after Matt Bell's May 6 repost. They came to you, don't burn it by outreaching too soon. Hold for 7-14 days minimum. Let Josh Pray content land Friday/Saturday so they see you operating at a level. Reach out from strength around May 16-20 with: 'Saw you followed the page after Matt's repost, wanted to introduce myself properly...' Premature outreach reads like a sales trigger and kills the warmth.

Outreach play (after May 16): casual text, not a pitch. 'Hey man, saw you followed the page, appreciate that. Been a minute, how's the shop doing?' Let HIM ask what you've been up to. Service fit: construction company = project showcase videos, time-lapse builds, brand spotlights, team/culture videos. Real video opportunity if he opens the door. Get name.

'Hey [Name], saw you followed the page, appreciated that. Hope [daughter's name] is doing well. If you ever want to grab coffee and chat about what we're doing for Explore Harrison, I'd love to.' Service fit: bank = community spotlight videos, customer testimonials, branch openings, employee features, sponsorship-coverage of local events. Don't pitch BVC immediately, this lead converts through relationship, not funnel. Get name.

Most local businesses can't see how invisible they are online — built a free 5-min checklist that walks through it. [BVC link]. Happy to chat if anything stands out.' Service fit: bank brand spotlights, leadership profiles, community involvement videos. Procurement cycle: 60-90 days minimum. Plant seed now, harvest later. Get name.

leads.ctx: Civic/tourism pricing only — NOT Entry Package. Airport managers handle community/tourism promotion and sometimes overlap with chambers and CVBs. May already work with Matt Bell or Toinette. Outreach play (after May 16): civic angle. 'Hi [Name], saw you followed @bray.films after Matt's repost. Been doing the work behind Explore Harrison and your operation came up in conversations more than once. Would love to connect if you're open to it.' Service fit: destination videos, event coverage, community-oriented promotional content. Possible play: co-pitch with Nikky Cagle if her partnership terms get locked. Get name.

leads.name: HPO Detail / Power Wash

voice.body: 'I've shot at Horseshoe Canyon multiple times' beats 'I shot at Horseshoe Canyon under previous ownership.' Don't pre-explain complications. Trust the reader.
voice.ctx: Letting facts stand without qualification reads confident. Pre-explaining reads anxious. Reader will ask if they care.

voice.rule: Frame work as a side effect, not the ask
voice.body: 'Possibly grab some footage while I'm at it' beats 'I'd love it to be on the production side.' Relationship is the primary ask, work is a maybe.
voice.ctx: Especially for warm intros and prior-relationship contacts. Even when the whole point is the work.

voice.rule: Exclamation points for warmth, not enthusiasm
voice.body: 'Looking forward to meeting you!' / 'if that's easier on your end!' These humanize the message, they're how you actually talk.
voice.ctx: Not sales-y. Not corporate. They sound like a real human who's looking forward to meeting another human.

voice.body: 'Bentley Ray' + phone + website is enough when there's any prior connection. Add 'Bray Films / Bentley Ray Media' only when the recipient needs a business identity to attach to.
voice.ctx: Cold prospect with no context = full business sign-off. Anyone with prior relationship or warm intro = personal sign-off. Mismatch reads weird.

voice.rule: 'Looking forward to meeting you' beats 'looking forward to talking'
voice.body: Personal language about the human, not the activity.
voice.ctx: Same for 'if that's easier on your end' vs 'if that's easier.' Always pull the language toward the person, away from the transaction.

preCallChecklist.sub: Know the 3 discovery questions cold before you dial
Pick up at 2:58pm CT — never late on a corporate buyer

whoHeIs.title: Who is Marcos Oliveira
whoHeIs.body: Senior Director of Lodging & Property Operations, Indigo Road Hospitality Group. New owners of Horseshoe Canyon Ranch (Jasper, AR).
whoHeIs.ctx:
This is a corporate buyer, not a local owner. Indigo Road runs boutique hotels and restaurants across the Carolinas, Charleston, and Asheville — brand-driven, design-conscious operators. He has brand standards, content vendors, and actual budget. Warm intro landed via Toinette Madison. He replied with 'Love it..' — that's interest, not a polite brushoff. The warm intro already filtered for fit. Don't over-explain yourself.

Indigo Road properties to recognize if they come up: The Dewberry (Charleston), Skyline Lodge (Highlands, NC), The Bedford (Houston). You don't need to know them deep — recognizing the names signals you did your homework.

pricingPosture.title: 💰 Pricing posture — anchor high, don't quote yet
pricingPosture.body: NOT Entry Package. Destination Brand Video: $1,500–$2,000. Monthly Retainer: $1,000–$1,500/mo. Don't quote on this call unless he asks directly.
pricingPosture.ctx:
$500 Entry Package is the wrong anchor for a hospitality group with multi-property operations. They'd lose respect for you. Read his appetite first:

If exploratory: propose a single destination brand video as the first engagement ($1,500–$2,000). Clean deliverable, low commitment, proves quality.

If serious about ongoing content: anchor at the upper end of the retainer range ($1,500/mo). Indigo Road owns the property long-term — one yes here is potentially years of recurring work.

New leverage: Matt Bell's public endorsement of Bray Films just went out. You have real social proof. Don't undersell.

discoveryQuestions.follow: Are they repositioning the brand? Adding rooms? Targeting weddings, adventure, corporate retreats? His answer tells you what the video needs to do.

discoveryQuestions.q: 2. "What content do you have right now, and what's missing?"
discoveryQuestions.follow: Lets him admit gaps without you pitching. If 'stills but no video' → easy in. If 'our Charleston agency handles it' → you're the local on-the-ground capability, not a replacement.

discoveryQuestions.q: 3. "If we did one thing first, what would have the biggest impact?"
discoveryQuestions.follow: Forces him to prioritize. His answer becomes your proposal. Common first deliverables: destination brand video, seasonal launch piece, cabin/room tour, event coverage.

toMention: Local — about an hour from the ranch. Can be onsite same-week if needed.
Already familiar with the property: know the light, the angles, the guest flow.
Working with Explore Harrison (Matt Bell) on regional tourism content — real social proof.
Open to walking the property when Marcos is next onsite.
doNotSay: Don't lead with price — let scope come first.
Don't pitch the Entry Package — wrong anchor for a corporate buyer.
Don't oversell the prior shoot — state it once, move on.
Don't apologize for being local or solo. The warm intro filtered for fit.
Don't talk about what you 'hope' to do. State what you do.
onTheCall: Open: "Hey Marcos, it's Bentley. Thanks for making time."
Let him drive the first 60 seconds. Match his pace.
Take notes on his exact words — those become your proposal language.
Before you hang up: if he wants a walk-through, lock the day and time on the call.
afterCall: Update Notion: stage → Proposal Sent (if scope clear) or Call Booked w/ updated notes.
Send a same-day follow-up email — 3 sentences max, confirm next step.
If a proposal is owed: use bray-films-proposal skill that night, ship within 24h.
Brief Toinette Madison — she made the intro, a 1-sentence update keeps the relationship warm.
